subject.title: feat(nodes): route alerts to the active computer

question: Should OpenClaw adopt Gateway-owned active-computer presence across node APIs, model context, and connection-alert routing as a permanent core contract?
rationale: The routing defects are mechanically repairable, but code review cannot decide whether the new authenticated activity event, public fields, prompt identity, and default cross-device delivery policy should become permanent product behavior.

options.title: Adopt after repair and proof
options.body: Approve the complete contract after all three routing defects are fixed, the conflict is resolved, and live multi-Mac evidence demonstrates active-first and fallback delivery.

options.title: Narrow the contract
options.body: Keep activity in node APIs and CLI while deferring model-context projection or automatic connection-alert routing.

options.title: Decline the direction
options.body: Close this PR and the canonical issue if active-computer telemetry and routing should not be core behavior.

recommendation.title: Adopt after repair and proof
recommendation.body: Approve the complete contract after all three routing defects are fixed, the conflict is resolved, and live multi-Mac evidence demonstrates active-first and fallback delivery.

likelyOwner.reason: Feature history, self-assignment, and repeated work across the affected macOS and node surfaces make this person the strongest available decision owner.
